summary.verdict: On claim discipline this page is ahead of every Best Hardware winner read for this coach. The Purpose section names the design that lost and why hardware answers it, the Results strip labels its own headline claims Partial and Untested with the reason in the same line, 7.1 separates Demonstrated from Not established and gives each gap the experiment that would close it, and 5.1 retracts a wrong specification in public, which nothing in either evidence bank does. Two things hold it back. It is 9,700 words against a winning range of 2,100 to 5,200, and the length is made of repetition: the loop is walked three times, the same five numbers appear in four places, the no-sampling claim is made eight times, and the calibration finding is told three times in one track. And the reproduction package does not survive a walk-through. The materials list cannot say what its own prices mean, does not contain the Luer valves, filters or transducers the assembly guide calls for, and is missing the tubing, cuvette, stirrer, droplet sensor, LED strip and photometer entirely; the guide stops after step eight; there is no sterilisation step, no file location and no licence; and nobody outside the team has touched the machine. Nine numbers also disagree with our own Digital Twin and photometer pages, and two of them, the cuvette path length and the longest run with the membrane fitted, change what the page claims.
strengths: The need argument. "A release problem became a containment problem, and containment is something hardware can solve." The rejected design is named, its failure mode is given as loss of control over expression, dose and spread, and the instrument follows from it. The research found no winner page, undergraduate or over, that derives a device from a rejected design this cleanly.

Results graded against themselves. Measured, Partial and Untested sit in the strip a judge reads first, and the labels are used against your own claims: breach detection is "Untested ... pressure transducers and a droplet sensor are fitted; no breach or alarm test is on record". No precedent in either bank puts a confidence label on a headline claim.

Limitations with the experiment attached. 7.1's "Not established" list and 7.2's Needs lines name eight gaps and what would close each one, down to "Containment with an n. Two platings, with no replicate count stated for either, and no incubation conditions for the first." Neither bioreactor precedent has a limitations section at all.

Arithmetic a reader can redo. Cycle 5 resolves an impossible rejection rate by showing 42.9% and 14.3% are 6 and 2 of a burst of 14, then writes out OD600 = -log[S / (K.R)] and shows one K near 9.16 reproducing all three dashboard snapshots. We checked it and it closes. Nothing in either bank publishes a reproducible calculation.

A retraction and a caveat in the same section. 5.1 withdraws the 50 kDa cut-off and the vesicle claim against the part actually bought, and 2.5 states what the 0.2 um pore does not stop. Saying what your own barrier passes is the move that makes a containment argument believable.
priorities: Settle the numbers with the Digital Twin team before anything is frozen. Four of them change claims: the cuvette path length (0.2 mm here and on the photometer page, 2 mm three times on the Twin page, whose factor-of-5.0 arithmetic supports 2 mm), the long run (past 400 hours with 2,132 points over 336 here, 434 hours with 2,671 valid rows there), its strain (WB800 here, 168 there, where that page says every reactor run before October used 168), and the longest run with the membrane fitted (53 h here, against a 102 h run on the full-length hollow fibre module there, inside which your 4 September dashboard snapshot sits).

Cut a third of the page, starting with the duplications. The loop is walked in the hero cards, in the arrow line in 2.5 and again in eight stages; 300 mL, 94 mL/min, 0.2 um and 200 rpm appear in four places; the in-line claim is repeated eight times; and cycle 6's finding is told in its Test, its Learn and its track box. Your hardware editor's rule is that if the prose and the box beneath it say the same thing, keep one. A judge will not read 9,700 words, which makes the Summary and Results strips the most valuable paragraphs on the page.

Make the materials list the list for this machine. Re-enter the sheet with quantity, unit cost, line total and a dated exchange rate, add the parts 6.2 and Table 4 require, and reconcile the counts: twelve Luer valves against five, four filters against one, four transducers against three, three reservoirs against two. Until then "Every line is costed, so the figure above is the build cost" is not true, and it sits two sentences from the admission that the sheet cannot be interpreted.

Finish the assembly guide, then say where the files are and under what licence. The guide ends with a vent filter and the machine is not built: no lumen-side plumbing, no culture reservoir, no photometer, no sensors, no LED strip, no priming, no sterilisation and no autoclave plan. This is the only one of our four hardware pages with no downloadable geometry, and none of the four states a licence on its designs.

Put one person outside the hardware team in front of the rig, and report what happened. Ballot question two is unanswered and 7.3 lists five items, none of which is a person. Having someone build the four membrane segments from 6.2 and write down where they got stuck answers the user-testing question and audits the documentation question in one afternoon.

ballot.question: Does the hardware you developed address a need or problem in synthetic biology?
ballot.note: The need is derived from a rejected transgenic design and ends on a requirement hardware can meet, which the research rated the best need argument in this page set, winners included.

ballot.question: Did the team conduct user testing and learn from user feedback?
ballot.note: No person outside the hardware sub-team is named anywhere on the page as having operated, assembled or reviewed the instrument, and 7.3's deployability list contains no person either.

ballot.question: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?
ballot.where: 3.1 Bacteria Growth, 3.2 cycle 5, 3.4 Bioreactor v1, 5.1 Containment
ballot.note: Two platings with no colonies, a plateau in two hours, a continuous run past 400 hours and a western blot are real functional evidence. Against that, the integrated run gets one sentence, the pressure and flow track is four empty headings, the flask comparison is uncontrolled, and the alarm path has never been tried against a deliberate fault.

ballot.question: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?
ballot.note: Three pump part numbers, a specification table traced to the run that produced each value, and a leak test with a fault tree, against a bill of materials that cannot say what its prices mean and does not match its own assembly guide, a guide that stops after step eight, no CAD or STL, no sterilisation, no software link and no licence.

releaf: Part 3 Engineering the Bioreactor, four tracks and nine cycles
winners: Need: what the work requires and what cannot do it now
Overview of the device, often as a short property list
Design and build, by prototype or by subsystem
Demonstration: one run that shows the device does its job
skeleton.gap: All five winner slots are present and three of them are stronger than any precedent: the need argument, the design history, and a Limitations part the winners do not have at all. The gap is where the weight sits. Slot four, the demonstration, is the slot four of five winners put last or second to last, and here it is one sentence in 3.4 buried inside a 9,700-word engineering record, while two of the four tracks that record is built on are empty headings. Slot five is positioned correctly and is the weakest content on the page. The practical move is to lift the integrated run and the containment platings into one demonstration block a judge meets early, and to spend the words saved on finishing Part 6.

extras: The hero figure's "Servo valveSwitches to the sampler" is the only mention of a servo valve on the page. The loop description gives a pinch valve on the return and dual Luer valves for sampling, and the materials list has neither a servo nor a pinch valve. Name the part that is fitted.
Section 2 runs 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.5. Either 2.4 was deleted or its number was skipped. Nothing cross-references 2.4, so no pointer is broken, but a judge counting sections will notice.

The Results row "Shell side grew no colonies ... the lumen plate beside one of them grew" stops mid-sentence. It does not say what the lumen plate grew, and that is the point: the plate that should grow did. Write "beside a lumen-side plate that grew colonies".

Growth cycle 1 reports "Final OD600 readings were 0.304 in the tube and 0.48 in the medium reservoir", and its own Figure 4 caption says the reactor went "from about 0.17 to 0.3-0.37 by the end of the run". Our Digital Twin page says "reactor 0.17 to 0.37". The 0.48 sits above all three.
Cycle 2 gives the flask plateau as OD600 about 0.6-0.8. Our Digital Twin page says "flask 0.83 by 278 min" and fits the flask arm reaching 0.83. Check both arms against the workbook.

Table 1's OD column reads 62.5 au for 2 mL of titanium dioxide, where Table 2 reads 0.5785 au for 2 mL in the same cell. The two tables cannot both be OD600 in the same units. Say what au is and how it is computed.

The three cycle 1 spacings (5.5 cm, 10 cm, 2 cm) are the fixed geometry for every later build and carry no tolerance, although V1 failed because loose mounts let that geometry drift. One tolerance per spacing is the thing a rebuilder cannot work out alone.
Cycle 6's Learn says "Test 1, 2-40 mg" where the fit label and the figure caption both say 2 to 41 mg, with n 39. One of the two is a typo.

Table 4's LED row gives green at about 526 nm. Our DiOPAL page says around 535 nm and our Math Model page says 535 nm activates CcaS; red is 670 here and 672 on the Math Model. Agree one pair across the wiki and cite it once.

Table 4 lists a "3 m green-light LED strip" and nothing else about it: no intensity at the vessel wall, no uniformity, no delivered dose, no part number. Humboldt measured light at 24 positions at three settings. One reading at the vessel wall, at the working setting, would do.

Section 5.1's whole argument rests on the B. subtilis diameter of 0.25 to 1.0 um, and no source is given for it. Cite the measurement, and say whether the 0.2 um figure is a nominal rating or an absolute one.

The blot band is at about 42 kDa here and our Math Model page gives the ACC deaminase subunit as 36.5 kDa, with a 144 kDa tetramer and a 9.4 nm hydrodynamic size. The 9.4 nm against a 200 nm pore is the number that supports "passes the protectant freely" in 2.5, and it is on the wrong page.
The segment list is in centimetres (7.5 cm) and the main assembly in inches (3-inch, 2-inch, 4-inch, 6-inch). Use one unit, because tube length sets the loop volume.

The stage walk in 2.5 is headed "as designed", and three of its parts are not in the build: the pinch valve is outlined for integration cycle 2, and the shell-side optical sensor and pH regulator have no line in the materials list. One word per stage, fitted or designed, settles it.
"Build" under growth cycle 2 and under photometer cycle 1 are empty headings. If the build is in the figure, say "As in Figure 6" so the heading is not blank.

Bioreactor v2 and v3 in 3.4 are headings with a cycle label and nothing else, and 3.4's "What it settled" box repeats its Learn line. One sentence each on what v2 and v3 would test, and the box can carry the one new clause.

"Filter parts 11 / 11 parts" and "No parts match that filter" are both rendered, so the filter control prints a contradiction in its default state. The list also has 11 line items against 12 component rows; say in the heading that the reference spectrophotometer is counted separately.
PES, BPT and TPU are each used without expansion, and PES is the membrane the whole device depends on. Expand each on first use.
"Illustrative: ... The machine is the compact B2 as proposed" is the only mention of a B2 on the page. Say what B2 is, or name the build the way 3.4 does.
"With a constrained timescale, the team could not complete everything it had in mind" apologises before naming the two goals. A judge only needs the goals.

Figure 25's caption calls the package "Three-channel" where the heading says three-chamber and the body says "single-channel prototype", and it introduces a camera that appears nowhere else on the page. Pick chamber or channel, and explain the camera or drop it.
The Summary says containment "rests on two platings of shell-side medium" and 7.1 says the same in its own words two parts later. One of the two can be a pointer.

notes.anchor: Either side of the membranePressure sensors ×4
notes.title: Four pressure sensors or three
notes.body: This panel says four, and Table 4 and section 3.3 name three, feed, retentate and permeate. The materials list in 6.1 has "Pressure sensor 3", while the assembly draft gives each of the four membrane segments "1x pressure transducer", which is four again. Count them on the rig and use one number in all four places.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: How it keeps the cells in
notes.title: These four numbers appear four times
notes.body: 300 mL, 94 mL/min, 0.2 um and 200 rpm are given here, again in the Summary strip, again in 2.5's two bullet lists and again in Table 4. Repetition is the thing your hardware editor asked you to cut hardest. Keep them in the Summary strip, where a judge who reads nothing else will see them, and drop this list.
notes.after:
How it keeps the cells in
One closed culture loop. One membrane wall. Nothing leaves it whole.

notes.anchor: Cells stay in. Protectant crosses.
notes.title: Two cards share one number
notes.body: This card and the one above it are both numbered 04, so the walk reads 01, 02, 03, 04, 04, 05, 06, and the route list above has six stops against seven cards. The two cards also say one thing. Merge them and the numbering fixes itself.
notes.after: The culture runs inside hollow fibres. Their walls have 0.2 µm pores, so cells stay in and protectant crosses.

notes.anchor: Illustrative: the liquids and everything that moves or glows
notes.title: The figure says what it assumed
notes.body: A moving diagram is the easiest place on a hardware page to overstate a device, and this credit line lists which parts of it are drawn and not measured, down to "flow direction assumed". It also says the machine shown is the proposed compact B2 and not the rig the results come from, which is the distinction a judge most needs.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen gives a full protocol and then says plainly what the experiment was not for. Same move: fence the claim before anyone over-reads it.

notes.anchor: Nine design‑build‑test‑learn cycles on one perfusion loop, from a prototype that leaked in June to an integrated run in September.
notes.title: The first line counts and admits
notes.body: One sentence gives the number of cycles, the span of months and the failure the work started from. A judge learns the shape of the record, and that you report what broke, before any claim arrives.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen's opening lands the need, the device and the reader in three sentences. Yours lands the scope and the honesty in one.

notes.anchor: The culture reached OD600 0.8–0.9 in two hours at 37 °C
notes.title: Four results in one paragraph
notes.body: This paragraph carries the growth result, the long photometer run, the western blot and the containment caveat in clauses joined by commas. A judge who reads only the summary has to unpick them. One sentence per claim, in the order the Results strip uses.
notes.after: The culture reached OD600 0.8-0.9 in two hours at 37 °C. The in-line photometer logged a culture for [hours] with no sampling event. ACC deaminase was detected on the shell side by western blot. Containment rests on two platings of shell-side medium, both of which grew no colonies, and neither states a replicate count.

notes.anchor: the in‑line photometer logged a culture past 400 hours with no sampling event
notes.title: Our own pages give this run two lengths
notes.body: Our Digital Twin page says "21 July to 8 August 2026: 434 hours of B. subtilis 168 at 22 °C, 2,671 valid rows, no sample drawn." This page and the photometer page say more than 400 hours with 2,132 points over the first 336. If it is one run, one page is wrong; if they are two windows of it, each page has to name its window, and this one should say what the hours after 336 show. The strain differs too, WB800 here and 168 there.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: the 0.2 µm pore stops whole cells and nothing smaller
notes.title: This sentence can be read two ways
notes.body: You mean the pore stops whole cells and lets everything smaller through. As written it also reads as "it stops whole cells, and it stops nothing smaller", which is the opposite of what 5.1 says. Two words fix it.
notes.after: the 0.2 µm pore stops whole cells and passes everything smaller

notes.anchor: Photometer needs no calibration Measured raw output within 4% of the BioDrop, across two TiO2 runs
notes.title: Say which number the four percent is
notes.body: Section 3.2 gives three figures for the same agreement: a median paired difference of 3.8% in test 2, a test 1 fit of y = 1.10x - 0.04, and an RMSE of 0.011 OD600. "Within 4%" is the first of those and it comes from one run, not two. Name the statistic and the run so a judge can find it.
notes.after: Photometer needs no calibration Measured raw output within a median 3.8% of the BioDrop in test 2, and a second TiO2 run agrees independently

notes.anchor: Breach detection Untested pressure transducers and a droplet sensor are fitted; no breach or alarm test is on record
notes.title: A headline row that says untested
notes.body: This row sits in the strip a judge reads first and it labels one of your own safety claims untested, with the reason in the same line. No page in either evidence bank puts a confidence label on a headline claim.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt reports an unfinished component in the same breath as its specification. You do it where it costs most, in the summary.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Fouling and service life Untested transmembrane pressure is logged; no fouling trend over a multi‑day run
notes.title: The strip mixes results with gaps
notes.body: Six rows, and three of them report a measurement while three report that no measurement exists. A judge scanning this cannot tell at a glance what the machine can do. Group the measured capabilities, each with its range, and put the untested items under one line of their own, which is how 7.1 already handles them.
notes.after: Not established yet Fouling and service life, breach detection, and how much product reaches the harvest stream (7.1).

notes.anchor: Our original design put the engineering in the soil.
notes.title: Two paragraphs before the point
notes.body: The first two paragraphs give the history and the third gives the argument, which is the strongest sentence on the page. On a 9,700-word page a judge may not reach it. One paragraph carries the same content and puts the payoff two sentences sooner.
notes.after: Our original design put the engineering in the soil: a transgenic plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium would colonize the roots and produce protectant where the plant needed it, with no delivery and no hardware. The flaw was control. Once a transgenic organism is released, expression, dose and spread are no longer ours to set, and the bacteria travel with soil and water.

notes.anchor: A release problem became a containment problem, and containment is something hardware can solve.
notes.title: The best sentence on the page
notes.body: The need argument names the design that lost, says what made it fail, and then says why hardware is the answer. Nothing in the five Best Hardware winners read for this coach derives an instrument from a rejected design this cleanly. Do not touch this paragraph.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt builds its need in four moves and ends on what a device would have to do. Yours gets there in one sentence.
notes.ballot: Does the hardware you developed address a need or problem in synthetic biology?

notes.anchor: Bacillus subtilis WB800 is well characterized, industrially proven, and native to the rhizosphere.
notes.title: Strain biology belongs to the wet lab
notes.body: Your editor cut the secretion paragraph off this page for this reason. The only part of this a hardware judge needs is the requirement the machine has to meet: the protectant is secreted, so separation is a size problem. Keep that and send the rest to the wet lab.
notes.after: B. subtilis WB800 secretes the protectant into the medium, so the product is already outside the cell and separation is a question of size.
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell lets the organism onto a hardware page only as a requirement: what it needs, next to what the part delivers.

notes.anchor: Many peptides degrade in storage, often require a cold chain, and lose potency before use.
notes.title: Two paragraphs that argue the market
notes.body: Section 1.3 argues shelf life, cold chain and freight cost, none of it hardware and none of it sourced. One sentence carries the consequence a hardware judge needs, which is that the machine has to make the protectant where it is used. The rest belongs on the project description or the entrepreneurship page.
notes.after: Many peptides degrade in storage and need a cold chain, so the protectant has to be made where it is used. That is the requirement this reactor is built against.

notes.anchor: The AIoT stage predicts plant stress and issues a light signal
notes.title: AIoT and LPA are never spelled out
notes.body: AIoT appears twice on this page and nowhere else in our page set, and it is never expanded. LPA in the next clause is not expanded either, and it is the name of one of our own instruments. Our judges read many pages a day and are not in our field.
notes.after: The stress-prediction stage (AIoT, artificial intelligence of things) predicts plant stress and issues a light signal; this bioreactor is the produce stage that receives it. The light-programmable array (LPA) is the instrument built to establish which light conditions drive protectant expression

notes.anchor: A batch reactor must be opened to be harvested, and every opening is a containment event and a contamination risk.
notes.title: This heading repeats the paragraph above
notes.body: Section 2.1 has already said that exchanging medium while the culture runs is the point of perfusion. The subheading then makes the same argument as a comparison. One paragraph holds both, and a judge meets the argument once.
notes.after: Exchanging medium while the culture runs is the point of perfusion: waste leaves, nutrients arrive, and the run does not have to stop. A batch reactor has to be opened to be harvested, and every opening is a containment event. Perfusion moves product out through a barrier that retains the organism, so the vessel stays closed from inoculation to shutdown. No medium feed was fitted in integration v1, so continuous exchange is not yet tested (7.1).

notes.anchor: All of it reports to one operator interface (Figure 21).
notes.title: This points three hundred lines ahead
notes.body: Figure 21 is the integration dashboard and it does not appear until 3.4, at the end of the engineering record; 3.3 points at it too. A reader in 2.3 cannot see the thing the monitoring claim rests on. Say what the interface shows, here, where the claim is made.
notes.after: All of it reports to one operator interface: OD600 with its sample and reference channels, flow rate, and feed, retentate and permeate pressure with the transmembrane pressure computed from them (3.4).

notes.anchor: Everything in the record below refers to one of two fluid paths. They meet only at the membrane wall.
notes.title: Two paths named before the detail
notes.body: This gives the reader the one abstraction the rest of the page depends on, in two short sentences, before a single component appears. Everything after it can then be placed by saying which side it sits on.
notes.excerpt_note: Humboldt's opening doubles as a specification sheet, so a reader can decide in one paragraph whether the instrument suits them. Yours does that job for the plumbing.

notes.anchor: Medium reservoir → peristaltic pump → in‑line photometer → fiber lumens → back to the reservoir.
notes.title: The loop is walked three times
notes.body: This arrow line gives the route in eleven words. The hero cards above walk it in seven panels and "The system, stage by stage" below walks it again in eight. Keep this line, and keep only the stages that add what it cannot: the harvest, the sensing and the delivery. Stages 1 to 4 repeat this sentence.
notes.after: Medium reservoir → peristaltic pump → in-line photometer → fiber lumens → back to the reservoir. Contains the organism, and is closed for the duration of the run; the only access is the dual Luer valve in the bill of materials, used for bleed and sampling.

notes.anchor: shell‑side medium plated in cycle 1 produced no colonies (5.1). The stream was cell‑free in both platings on record.
notes.title: Two sentences, one fact
notes.body: These say the same thing twice, once about cycle 1 and once about both platings. Keep the second, which carries more and still points at 5.1.
notes.after: Anything in that stream crossed the fiber wall, whose 0.2 µm pore is smaller than a B. subtilis cell; the stream was cell-free in both platings on record (5.1).

notes.anchor: Shell‑side fluid passes a pH regulator on its way out to the delivery stages.
notes.title: The pH regulator is never specified
notes.body: This stage is one sentence and the regulator appears nowhere else on the page: no part, no setpoint, no reagent, no line in the materials list. The hero figure says "pH controlKOH pump". If KOH is the reagent, say so here and put the pump in 6.1.
notes.after: Shell-side fluid passes a pH regulator on its way out to the delivery stages. It holds the product stream at [setpoint] by dosing [reagent] with the [part] pump.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: The loop ran at room temperature. The peristaltic pump reached the target flow rate of 94 mL/min, but the trial ended early when medium leaked at the pump.
notes.title: Lead with the thing that ended the run
notes.body: The paragraph opens on the flow rate holding, puts the leak in a subordinate clause, and then calls the OD readings final. A reader meets the numbers before learning the run was cut short, so "final" reads as a planned endpoint. Put the leak first.
notes.after: The loop ran at room temperature and ended early when medium leaked at the pump head. Up to that point the peristaltic pump held the target 94 mL/min. The last OD600 readings before the stop were 0.304 in the tube and [value] in the medium reservoir (Figure 4).

notes.anchor: Single plating; replicate count and incubation time and temperature were not recorded (5.1).
notes.title: A caption that states its own n
notes.body: Only one page in either evidence bank puts measurement conditions in its captions, and none of them lists the conditions that were not recorded. This clause costs you nothing and it is why a judge will believe the rest of your platings.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt is the only precedent whose captions carry measurement conditions. Yours carry the missing ones too.

notes.anchor: The divergent OD600 values between the tube and the reservoir indicated poor growth and pointed to two hardware limitations for the next cycle.
notes.title: Two limitations, then three fixes
notes.body: The paragraph promises two hardware limitations and then lists three changes: BPT tubing, a magnetic stirrer and a moved sampling port. Name the faults, then the fix for each, in the same order.
notes.after: The divergent OD600 values between the tube and the reservoir pointed to two faults: no active mixing in the reservoir, and a seal that leaked at the pump head. We planned a magnetic stirrer for the first, on the model of a laboratory hot-plate stirrer, and biocompatible BPT tubing for the second. We also moved the sampling port to the reservoir outlet, for a cleaner reading and less contamination risk.

notes.anchor: the bioreactor reached its plateau (OD600 ~0.8–0.9) after 2 hours, the flask (OD600 ~0.6–0.8) after 4.5 hours
notes.title: Say what would have counted as success
notes.body: The run is reported without a criterion set beforehand, so a reader cannot tell whether plateau in two hours was the target or a surprise. Aachen's chemostat states the pass condition before the result. One clause before these numbers does the same work here.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen fixes the criterion first: hold each dilution rate for three reactor volumes and see whether OD stays constant within sampling error. The reader knows what would have counted as failure.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Both arms used the same medium and temperature, but that is not a controlled comparison.
notes.title: You take your own result apart
notes.body: The comparison is set up and then disarmed in the same section: the three unrecorded flask variables are named, the three-variables-at-once problem is stated, and the reader is told how far to trust it. "A promising difference, not a measured one" is the sentence a judge will quote back.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen fences off a sensor test so nobody reads it as a bioprocess result. You fence off your own headline growth claim.

notes.anchor: These are its design–build–test–learn cycles; the instrument itself, part by part, has its own record.
notes.title: Put the pointer before the track
notes.body: This clause tells the reader that part-level detail lives elsewhere, and it arrives at the end of the paragraph that opens a track running nearly two hundred lines. Anyone looking for a part number has read the whole track by then. Move it to the first line.
notes.after: The in-line flow-cell photometer is the optical-density monitoring subsystem of the bioreactor; the instrument itself, part by part, has its own record. What follows is its design-build-test-learn cycles.

notes.anchor: Adjustability helped during alignment and hurt everywhere else.
notes.title: A design rule from one build
notes.body: Nine words turn a build annoyance into a rule another team can use, and the paragraph above it has already given the mechanism. This is the move the 2024 undergraduate winner was rewarded for.
notes.excerpt_note: UBC turns a printer tolerance problem into a transferable design rule. Same shape, shorter.

notes.anchor: The optics were not the main problem. Our calibration procedure was.
notes.title: A diagnosis that corrects yourselves
notes.body: Two short sentences, then the mechanism: you blanked on growth medium, the BioDrop on distilled water, so a gap you had been blaming on your own optics was procedural. The protocol that came out of it is stated in the next line and used from then on.
notes.excerpt_note: TU Darmstadt reports its instrument reading low and then explains the mechanism in its own calibration. Yours finds the error in the procedure and says so.

notes.anchor: the roughly 20% disagreement we had been attributing to our optics was largely a procedural artifact
notes.title: The twenty percent is not on the page
notes.body: This is the only mention of a 20% disagreement, and no table in cycles 1 to 3 shows it. A judge cannot check the finding your whole calibration protocol came out of. Give the two readings it was computed from, or say where they are recorded.
notes.after: the roughly 20% disagreement we had been attributing to our optics, [our reading] against the BioDrop's [reading], was largely a procedural artifact

notes.anchor: Photometer · Cycle 4
notes.title: A version is missing from the list
notes.body: The builds run V1, V2, an unnumbered "Angled stand", then V4. There is no V3 anywhere on the page. If the angled stand is V3, call it V3. If it is not, say what V3 was, because a reader meeting V4 after V2 assumes a build was dropped from the record.
notes.after: Photometer · Cycle 4 · V3

notes.anchor: Doubling the titanium dioxide only moved the reading by a factor of 1.56, which we cannot yet explain from this data alone.
notes.title: Name the two explanations you have
notes.body: Saying you cannot explain it is right. A judge would rather see the candidates, and two sit in your own record: the open light path this same paragraph blames for the reference drift, and the compression at high turbidity the photometer page describes. Name both and leave them unresolved.
notes.after: Doubling the titanium dioxide only moved the reading by a factor of 1.56. Two candidates sit in this record, stray room light reaching the sample sensor and compression of the reading at high turbidity, and this run cannot separate them.
notes.excerpt_note: TU Darmstadt gives the threshold above which a reading is usable and draws the general rule. A named limit beats a general caution.

notes.anchor: The run covers lag through decline in one unbroken series, which is the thing a manual sampling routine cannot produce.
notes.title: The Twin page calls the decline a fault
notes.body: Our Digital Twin page says of this run "the OD channel failed" and marks a sensor alarm at 216.3 h, which falls inside the 336 h traced here. If the late decline is the instrument and not the culture, this series cannot be read as lag through decline. Settle which hours are trustworthy and put the answer in Figure 16's caption.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: The dashboard expects a sample‑to‑reference ratio near 10:1 and we measured 5.3× to 6.4×, so either the split ratio or the expectation is wrong.
notes.title: Say which splitter is fitted
notes.body: Our photometer page says a 90:10 splitter and our Digital Twin page says the splitter ran at 9:1. Both come to the 10:1 expectation, and your measurement is about half of it. Name the part and its rated split, so a reader can tell whether the part or the expectation is at fault.
notes.after: The dashboard expects a sample-to-reference ratio near 10:1, set by the [part] splitter rated at [split], and we measured 5.3x to 6.4x, so either the part or the expectation is wrong.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: with the factor, all three snapshots above reproduce with one K ≈ 9.16
notes.title: A formula a reader can check
notes.body: The calculation is written out and then shown to reproduce every row of the table above it. We redid it: 171.67 over 9.16 times 26.67 gives 0.153, and five times that is 0.765 against the 0.7661 on the dashboard. Nothing in either evidence bank publishes a reproducible calculation like this.
notes.excerpt_note: TU Darmstadt gives the correlation coefficient and the transform it fitted. You give the formula and show it closing on your own data.

notes.anchor: plotted as RELEAF against BioDrop, Test 1 has a slope near 1 and an intercept near 0
notes.title: Near one hides a ten percent gap
notes.body: The fit printed under this sentence is y = 1.10x - 0.04. A slope of 1.10 means the two instruments differ by about 10% at the top of the range, which is not "near 1" for a reader who is about to trust a reading. Give the number and what it costs.
notes.after: plotted as RELEAF against BioDrop, Test 1 gives a slope of 1.10 and an intercept of -0.04, so our reading runs about 10% above the BioDrop at the top of the range

notes.anchor: RELEAF photometer y = 0.03x + 0.0448 · R² 0.9999 · n 18BioDrop y = 0.0318x + 0.00163 · R² 0.9998 · n 19
notes.title: The excluded point comes off the wrong fit
notes.body: Test 2's exclusion is a BioDrop reading, so the BioDrop fit should be the one that loses a point. Here the BioDrop has n 19 and RELEAF n 18. The direct-agreement fit below it also has n 19, and a paired plot cannot hold more points than its shorter series. Check all three counts against the workbook.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Two properties emerged from this cycle.
notes.title: This paragraph repeats the Learn above it
notes.body: The first property restates agreement already given twice in this cycle. The second, that the instrument reads in line without withdrawing a sample, is stated in 2.3, in stage 2 of 2.5, in the Results strip and again in 7.1. Keep the one clause none of them has.
notes.after: A cuvette spectrophotometer cannot monitor a live bioreactor; it measures grab samples one at a time. Cycle 5 showed this instrument reading the same culture continuously, which is what closed-loop monitoring needs.

notes.anchor: The calibration transform this track was built to produce turned out to be unnecessary.
notes.title: The third telling of one finding
notes.body: This box repeats the Learn paragraph of cycle 6, which repeats the Test paragraph above it. A track summary earns its place by saying something the cycles did not, for example which build the photometer in the final design is.
notes.after: The calibration transform this track was built to produce turned out to be unnecessary, so no transform is applied to any reading here. The photometer in the final design is [version].

notes.anchor: Four cycles are outlined here and none has been run.
notes.title: The dashboard already has the numbers
notes.body: Four empty cycles sit above a figure that logs feed, retentate and permeate pressure, and Table 4 reports all three from 4 September. Report that one reading here, with the flow it was taken at, and the track stops being empty. Aachen shows the shape for a single control observation: what was set, how long it held, what changed and what it did to the measurement.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen reports a pump imbalance found mid-run in sequence, with the correction and its measured cost in OD. One paragraph, and the reader trusts the rig.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Engineered B. subtilis was run in the system and ACC deaminase was secreted across the membrane (Figure 22).
notes.title: The one integrated run gets one line
notes.body: This is the demonstration the proof-of-concept question turns on, and it is a single sentence whose caption carries more than it does. Give the run its conditions here: strain, medium, volume, temperature, duration and flow. The strain matters most, because 3.1 names WB800 and our Digital Twin page names 168 with the v2t1 construct.
notes.after: Engineered B. subtilis [strain] was run in the loop in [medium] at [temperature] for [duration] at 94 mL/min, and ACC deaminase was detected in shell-side medium sampled from 14 to 44 h (Figure 22).
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt's culture test gives volume, inoculum, strain, time and the one observation it supports. One paragraph, then back to hardware.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: ACC deaminase was successfully secreted to the shell side, but expression is weak.
notes.title: Weak against what
notes.body: "Weak" has no reference here. A blot band is weak relative to a loading control, to the lumen-side lanes or to a standard. Say which comparison you mean and what the next measurement would be. Section 7.2 already names it, so the pointer is written.
notes.after: ACC deaminase reached the shell side. The band is faint against the lumen-side lanes on the same blot, so the amount crossing is small and has not been quantified (7.2).

notes.anchor: The values below are the ones stated elsewhere in this record and in the draft assembly guide (6.2)
notes.title: Specifications traced to their run
notes.body: Both bioreactor precedents state their specifications as settled facts without saying which run established them. This sentence, and the cycle pointer in each row, make the table an audit of the record instead of a claim about the machine. The rows that disagree with themselves are visible because of it.
notes.excerpt_note: Humboldt's opening gives configurations, volumes and ranges as a specification sheet. Yours adds the provenance theirs leaves out.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: about 371 mL/min on the 4 September integration‑v1 dashboard (Figure 21)
notes.title: Two flow rates, four times apart
notes.body: Recording both without choosing is honest, and it leaves a reader unable to use either. 94 mL/min appears five times elsewhere on the page as the flow rate. Say which is the design setting and what the other one was: a different pump, a different tube bore, or a dashboard reading in different units.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Feed, retentate and permeate read about 0.20 bar each on the 4 September dashboard
notes.title: Equal pressures mean zero TMP
notes.body: If all three read 0.20 bar, the transmembrane pressure computed from them is about zero, and 3.3 calls TMP the record's highest open parameter. Either the figures are rounded past the difference that matters, or the transducers were reading the same point. Give the three values to the precision the dashboard shows, the TMP that follows, and the range you would accept on a clean module.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Making sure synthetic organisms do not enter the wild is a responsibility for everyone working with genetically modified organisms.
notes.title: Two sentences that say nothing yet
notes.body: This opening states that biosafety matters and that it matters to us. The section's real claim is much stronger and arrives one heading later: containment here is physical, at a pore smaller than the cell. Start there.
notes.after: Containment in this reactor is physical. The only thing holding B. subtilis inside the machine is a membrane whose pores are smaller than the cells.

notes.anchor: From shell‑side medium, in both platings on record: cycle 1, and a lumen‑and‑shell comparison in which the lumen plate grew.
notes.title: The number arrives before the test
notes.body: This block opens the section with a result and two figure pointers for a test the reader has not met. The principle and the test are both just below it. Lead with the barrier and the test, and let the zero land after them, where it means something.
notes.after: Containment is by size exclusion at the membrane, and it was tested directly: medium from both sides of the running reactor was plated and compared. No colonies grew from the shell side, in either plating on record.

notes.anchor: An earlier version of this specification claimed a 50 kDa molecular‑weight cut‑off and stated that the membrane retains secreted membrane vesicles.
notes.title: A retraction, in public, with the reason
notes.body: Nothing in either evidence bank retracts anything. This paragraph names the wrong claim, says why it was wrong for the part actually bought, draws the consequence that containment now rests on cell size alone, and dates the withdrawal. A judge who finds this believes the rest of the page.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen reports a second, worse result instead of dropping it, and grades the degradation. Yours reports a wrong claim instead of deleting it.

notes.anchor: Neither has been tried against a deliberate leak or a deliberate breach, so the alarm path is not yet tested (7.1).
notes.title: Both alarms are an afternoon's test
notes.body: You name this gap exactly, and it is the cheapest result left on the page. A few drops of water under the droplet sensor, and a loosened Luer fitting with the pressure log running, each with the response written down. You already have the shape in 6.2's own leak test, and TUDarmstadt's reproduction package is a leak test and an air test with a stated result each.
notes.excerpt_note: UBC sets a target, measures against it, and reports what the measurement turned out to depend on. A pass condition is what makes a safety test reportable.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Every line is costed, so the figure above is the build cost.
notes.title: This cannot be the build cost
notes.body: Two sentences later the page says "The sheet does not say whether a price is per unit or per line". If the prices are per unit, four pumps at 2,500 come to 10,000 and the parts total is wrong. The list also has no tubing, no flow cuvette, no droplet sensor, no magnetic stirrer, no LED strip, no pinch valve and no photometer, all of which 6.2 and Table 4 require. NT$16,450 is a column total, not the cost of this machine.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Costs are as entered on the team's component sheet, in New Taiwan dollars.
notes.title: Re-enter the sheet with unit costs
notes.body: Being honest about an ambiguous sheet is better than hiding it, and the fix is one afternoon. Four columns close it: quantity, unit cost, line total, and the date of the exchange rate. Aachen scopes its estimate in a sentence before the numbers, and Humboldt gives seven subsystem lines to one figure a team can hold against its own budget.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen names what is being totalled before totalling it. Humboldt gives the reason for publishing a price before the price.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: The sheet does not say whether a price is per unit or per line
notes.title: The caveat arrives after the total
notes.body: The block above prints NT$16,450 and the sentence "Every line is costed, so the figure above is the build cost", and the qualification only turns up here, under the table. US$960 is also about NT$30,450, the total with the spectrophotometer, and not the figure called the build cost. Say what the number is before giving it.
notes.after: The sheet does not say whether a price is per unit or per line, so the figure below is the sum of its cost column and not a verified build cost. Costs are as entered on the team's component sheet, in New Taiwan dollars: NT$16,450 for the parts, NT$30,450 with the reference spectrophotometer, about US$960 at the sheet's own rate on [date].
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell qualifies its bill of materials in the sentence straight after it, which is why its headline price is believable.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: The build, segment by segmentworking draft
notes.title: No files and no licence for the build
notes.body: This is the only one of our four hardware pages with no downloadable geometry, and none of the four states a licence on its designs. The dashboard is unnamed here too, while our Digital Twin page credits "the Arduino App Lab application our instructor Chars wrote for the Uno Q board on BR-01" at interface v4.13. Aachen 2015 carries a licence in every footer and releases its control software under GPL v3; Humboldt puts assembly instructions, parts list and software in one tagged release.
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell names the deliverable another team needs and itemises what is in it. One sentence, and the reader knows what to download.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: One segment connects each of the membrane's four ports
notes.title: The two parts lists do not add up
notes.body: Four segments at two Luer valves each is eight, plus the four in the main assembly list is twelve, against "Luer valve 5" in 6.1. Each segment also takes one filter and one pressure transducer, which is four of each, against "Air filter 1" and "Pressure sensor 3". The reservoirs are a third case: two 1 L and a 100 mL here, "Reservoir 2" in 6.1, and a 500 mL vessel in Table 4. A reader buying from 6.1 cannot build the segments in 6.2.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Cut the tubing into three sections, A, B and C.
notes.title: Say how long each section is
notes.body: The segment list gives 7.5 cm of tubing and three sections and never says how to divide it. It also never gives the tubing bore, which is what decides the flow the pump delivers. Two numbers here make the segment buildable.
notes.after: Cut the 7.5 cm of tubing into three sections: A at [length], B at [length] and C at [length], all of [bore] inner bore.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Hold the right port facing up and feed 3–5 drops of water into it with a dropper, then slowly rotate the handle of the center valve and watch for leaks.
notes.title: A check written for someone holding it
notes.body: The quantity, the orientation, the action, then the fault tree, in two sentences and in the second person. This is the best-written passage in the reproduction section and it is the register the rest of the guide needs.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen's construction steps tell a reader what to glue where and what changes between builds. Same voice.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Connect the other end of the In‑Shell segment to one end of the flow cuvette with a 3‑inch tube.
notes.title: Which optical device is this
notes.body: This step puts the flow cuvette on the In-Shell segment. Section 2.5 puts the photometer's flow cell in the culture loop, on the lumen side, and gives the shell side a separate "optical sensor". The materials list has one flow cuvette and no optical sensor. Say which instrument this step fits and which side it reads, because a shell-side stream has no cells in it to measure.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Connect a 2‑inch tube from the “Out” of a filter to another hole in the cap of the shell‑side reservoir.
notes.title: The guide stops after eight steps
notes.body: This is the last step, and the machine is not built: no lumen-side plumbing, no culture reservoir, no photometer, no pH sensor, no droplet sensor, no stirrer placement, no LED strip and no priming. TUDarmstadt publishes seven numbered steps with a photograph each. Finishing this from material already on the page is the single biggest thing you can do for the reproduction question.
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell names its operating manual and itemises it: assembly, operation, precautions, and the differences between variants.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Containment with an n. Two platings, with no replicate count stated for either, and no incubation conditions for the first.
notes.title: The gap named as an experiment
notes.body: Every line of "Not established" names the claim, the evidence under it and what is missing, and this one turns the missing thing into something a reader could go and do. Neither bioreactor precedent has a limitations section at all. This is the strongest section on the page.
notes.excerpt_note: Humboldt converts a validation plot into a working range and says what would extend it. Yours does that for eight claims at once.

notes.anchor: A multi-day run with the photometer logging continuously, to establish that the loop is stable over the timescale a field deployment needs.
notes.title: Nobody outside the team has touched it
notes.body: Five items here, and not one of them is a person. Ballot question two asks about user testing, and nobody outside the hardware sub-team is named anywhere on this page. The cheapest answer is one person building the four membrane segments from 6.2 and writing down where they got stuck, which audits the documentation question in the same afternoon. UBC ran five sessions on a bioreactor of its own and named the testers and their expertise.
notes.excerpt_note: UBC writes user testing as an event with a place, a date, a named contact outside the team and a count of sessions.
notes.ballot: Did the team conduct user testing and learn from user feedback?

notes.anchor: The three‑chamber concept arose while we were researching which protectants our B. subtilis should produce and secrete.
notes.title: The protectant search is wet lab
notes.body: Two paragraphs here explain how three protectants were chosen and which stresses they target. That argument belongs to the wet lab and to the Protein Design page. The hardware consequence is one sentence.
notes.after: Three protectants mean three isolated cultures, each with its own light. That is the three-chamber concept: three compartments, switched green or red to set which protectant is made and secreted.

notes.anchor: ACC deaminase, LEA peptide and BoPep4
notes.title: Two protectant names are wrong
notes.body: Our Protein Design pages write BoPEP4 throughout, and the LEA molecule is LEA14, which those pages call "the ordered/globular protein LEA14" and deliberately distinguish from the disordered peptides in the family. "LEA peptide" and "BoPep4" appear only here. Use the names the wet lab uses.
notes.after: ACC deaminase, LEA14 and BoPEP4

notes.anchor: Nothing here has been built — it is the packaged arrangement the single‑channel prototype is a step toward
notes.title: A CAD figure labelled unbuilt
notes.body: A rendered concept is the easiest place on a hardware page to mislead a judge, and this caption says in its first clause that nothing in the image exists. It then says what the figure is for, which is the volume the machine would have to fit into.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt reports a component unfinished in the same paragraph as its specification. Yours labels a whole figure as unbuilt.

resolved.anchor: the longest run with the membrane module fitted is about 53 hours (7.2)
resolved.title: Our Twin page has a longer membrane run
resolved.body: The Digital Twin page lists run 4, 1 to 6 September, as "168 with constitutive ACC deaminase secretion, in the incubator, full-length hollow fibre module" and "102 h from 0.84 to 3.77". Figure 21 here is dated 4 September and captioned "53 h into a recording", which falls inside that window. If they are the same run, your longest membrane run is about 102 hours and this sentence halves your own best result.
resolved.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

resolved.anchor: Culture B. subtilis WB800 at room temperature (22 °C)
resolved.title: The strain here may be the wrong one
resolved.body: Our Digital Twin page says "Every reactor run before October used B. subtilis 168" and lists both June runs as 168, where both headers in 3.1 say WB800. The two pages cannot both be right about June. Check the lab record and write one strain on both pages, because the strain is part of every growth number here.
resolved.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

resolved.anchor: B. subtilis WB800; engineered strains in the 400 h run and integration v1
resolved.title: No sterilisation anywhere in the guide
resolved.body: Section 6.3 gives the organism, the medium, the inoculum and the temperature, and nothing on the page says how any of it is sterilised or which parts survive an autoclave. The membrane cartridge, the printed photometer body and the pumps cannot go in together. The medium needs the same treatment: LB has several recipes and the page never says which, or whether it carries an antibiotic, where our Digital Twin page says the WB800 repeat ran "under antibiotic selection".
resolved.excerpt_note: Cornell lists its materials and justifies them by one consequence: the assembly can be autoclaved, so a dedicated autoclave configuration was designed. Biology enters a hardware page as a constraint.
resolved.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

resolved.anchor: The longest recording known to have the membrane module fitted is about two days (53 h, integration cycle 1).
resolved.title: Check this against run four
resolved.body: The Digital Twin page's run 4 is logged with the "full-length hollow fibre module" and runs 102 hours, 2 to 6 September. Figure 21 here is a 4 September snapshot at 53 h, which falls inside that window. If they are the same run, this line and 1.2 both understate your best membrane run by half, and the open parameter in this block is partly answered already.
resolved.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

resolved.anchor: The 400 h photometer record was drawn from the bioreactor loop, in the doc's words.
resolved.title: In the doc's words is not a source
resolved.body: "The doc" appears in 4.1, in 6.1 and here, and the page never says what it is or where a reader could see it. If it is an internal working document, cite it by name and date. If the claim is yours, own it, and say whether the membrane module was fitted for that run, because that is the question this block is asking.
resolved.after: The 400 h photometer record was drawn from the bioreactor loop, recorded in [document, date]. The membrane module [was or was not] fitted for it.

resolved.anchor: passing the culture through a flow cuvette with a 0.2 mm path
resolved.title: Our Twin page says ten times this
resolved.body: This page and the photometer page say a 0.2 mm path. The Digital Twin page says a 2 mm flow cuvette three times, and its own arithmetic supports 2 mm: "a path length factor of 5.0, so a 2 mm cell is reported on a 1 cm equivalent scale", and 10 mm over 2 mm is 5. At 0.2 mm that factor would be 50, and your own cycle 5 notes record the dashboard reporting five times the computed value. Path length scales OD directly, so measure the cuvette and write one figure on all three pages.
resolved.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?
